llm.summary: This is a local-only note and document-organizing HTML tool with disclosed clipboard, file, and browser storage behavior.

dimensions.detail: The HTML uses browser APIs for paste, drag-and-drop, user-selected file reads, object URL downloads, localStorage, and IndexedDB, all proportionate to an offline note/file board; no network calls, credential access, or background workers were found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill points users to open assets/word-doc.html directly or package the directory with a skill-creator script; there is no automatic installer, dependency install, or hidden execution path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The routing text is somewhat broad for note-taking and clipboard organization requests, but the actual instructions consistently describe the same local HTML deliverable and disclose its storage and file-handling features.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Notes and metadata persist in localStorage and images/files persist in IndexedDB until the user deletes them; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users should understand local browser storage retention.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a single-file offline board for collecting text, managing user-provided images/files, and exporting DOCX; the bundled HTML implements those capabilities without unrelated behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an offline browser-based note board that stores pasted text, selected files, and images in your browser. Do not treat its local storage as encrypted or shared-device safe, and clear the browser data or the app's recycle/draft areas when you no longer want retained content.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad description could cause over-invocation, but it is a routing-quality concern rather than evidence of hidden or purpose-mismatched behavior; the artifact clearly presents a local single-file note board.
[SQP-1] expected: The when-to-use section covers common productivity cases, and the active HTML features cited by the scanner are disclosed capabilities needed for clipboard capture, drag-and-drop, local storage, and DOCX export.
